# Event counters and de-bounce against a REAL signal on PA3.
#
# Captured 2026-08-26 on the bench, through the benchctrl agent over RPC
# (not a direct driver open — the agent holds the device, and a second open
# correctly fails with "interface 0 is busy", KNOWN_LIMITATIONS § N-4).
#
# Stimulus: Siglent SDG1032X square wave into PA3, driven manually by the
# operator. The SDG1032X has no driver yet, which is why the stimulus is
# operator-set rather than scripted -- and that is the better split here: a
# harness that changed the signal while measuring it could not tell a
# de-bounce effect from a generator change.
#
# Nothing was switched. Watchdog left disarmed (WD0) throughout. De-bounce was
# restored to its entry value (1) at the end.
#
# WHY THIS FIXTURE EXISTS: before this capture, no ADU218 input line had ever
# been driven to a 1 on this bench, so no counter had ever incremented and
# clear_counter() had never run on the device. The inputs/counters/de-bounce
# half of the driver was implemented and simulator-covered but unwitnessed.

=== PA3 at ~0.5 Hz: two independent methods, 30.010 s window ===
# Method A: the device's own counter (RE3).
# Method B: host-side level sampling of RPA3, counting transitions.
# Distinct failure modes: the counter can see edges the host never samples,
# and the host sampler aliases if the wave is fast vs the ~17 ms round trip.

debounce setting: 1
window        : 30.000 s
host samples  : 1712  (mean interval 17.5 ms -> Nyquist limit ~28.5 Hz)

--- Method A: device event counter RE3 ---
  15 counts in 30.000 s  => 0.500 counts/s

--- Method B: host level sampling ---
  15 rising, 15 falling edges seen  => 0.500 rising edges/s
  duty cycle: 859/1712 high = 50.2 %

--- comparison ---
  A/B = 1.000

--- shape: consecutive-sample run lengths ---
  high runs: n=15  mean=57.3  (~1004 ms mean)
  low  runs: n=15  mean=53.3  (~934 ms mean)
  single-sample runs: 0 (clean)

=== PA3 at ~10 Hz: the same two methods, 30.010 s window ===

debounce setting: 1
window        : 30.010 s
host samples  : 1687  (mean interval 17.8 ms -> Nyquist limit ~28.1 Hz)

--- Method A: device event counter RE3 ---
  3206 -> 3507   = 301 counts in 30.010 s
  => 10.030 counts/s

--- Method B: host level sampling ---
  300 rising, 300 falling edges seen
  => 9.997 rising edges/s
  duty cycle: 905/1687 high = 53.6 %

--- comparison ---
  A/B = 1.003

--- shape: consecutive-sample run lengths ---
  601 runs total
  high runs: n=301  min=1  max=4  mean=3.0  (~53 ms mean)
  low  runs: n=300  min=1  max=3  mean=2.6  (~46 ms mean)
  single-sample runs: 63

# NOTE on those 63 single-sample runs: that is the HOST SAMPLER aliasing, not
# bounce on the wire. At 17.8 ms per sample against a 50 ms half-period only
# ~3 samples land per half-cycle, so a boundary sample forming a run of 1 is
# routine. The device counter is unaffected. Compare the 0.5 Hz run above,
# where ~57 samples per half-cycle gave 0 single-sample runs. At 10 Hz the
# device counter is the method to trust; Method B is a sanity check only.

# CONCLUSION, and the reason A/B matters more than either number alone:
# A/B = 1.003 at 10 Hz and 1.000 at 0.5 Hz. The counter increments ONCE PER
# CYCLE, not once per edge -- had it counted both edges A/B would be 2.0.
# Manual §6c agrees in words ("count low to high transitions"), but this is
# the measurement, at two frequencies an order of magnitude apart.

=== counter-to-input map: only counter 3 moves ===
# The map is documented ONLY in a Table 1 IMAGE that pdftotext drops
# entirely -- the extraction renders blank space where the table should be.
# So this could not be read from the manual at all, only measured.

input_states :  {'A': [False, False, False, True], 'B': [False, False, False, False]}
input_mask   :  0b00001000

  t=0.00s  counters read
  t=2.00s  counters read again

  deltas over ~2.0 s:
    counter 0:     0 ->     0  delta     +0
    counter 1:     0 ->     0  delta     +0
    counter 2:     0 ->     0  delta     +0
    counter 3:    97 ->    98  delta     +1   <-- COUNTING
    counter 4:     0 ->     0  delta     +0
    counter 5:     0 ->     0  delta     +0
    counter 6:     0 ->     0  delta     +0
    counter 7:     0 ->     0  delta     +0

# PA3 -> counter 3, and nothing else. Confirms the driver's assumed mapping
# (counters 0-3 -> PA0-PA3, 4-7 -> PB0-PB3) for the one line under stimulus.
# The B-port half of the map remains untested on hardware.

=== RCn is genuinely read-and-clear ===
  RE3 before  : 98
  RC3 returned: 98      (the value it cleared)
  RE3 after   : 0

# The residual would have been non-zero had more edges arrived during the
# round trip; at 0.5 Hz it did not. This is the command that must never be
# retried: a lost reply loses the count permanently and a retry returns 0,
# indistinguishable from "no events happened".

=== B4: de-bounce ladder against the 10 Hz signal, 20 s per setting ===
# Only DB varies. Stimulus untouched between settings.

  DB0:   201 counts in 20.02 s =  10.042 counts/s   (100.4% of 10.0 Hz)
  DB1:   200 counts in 20.02 s =   9.992 counts/s   ( 99.9% of 10.0 Hz)
  DB2:   200 counts in 20.02 s =   9.992 counts/s   ( 99.9% of 10.0 Hz)

  spread: 0.5% between the extremes  -> INDISTINGUISHABLE

  restored de-bounce to 1

# This is a NEGATIVE RESULT WITH A KNOWN SCOPE, not a finding that DB is inert.
#
# Manual §6c gives the durations: 0 = 10ms, 1 = 1ms (default), 2 = 100us.
# Note the INVERSION -- a higher setting is a SHORTER filter. At 10 Hz the
# half-period is 50 ms, so all three filters are shorter than the interval
# between transitions and none of them has anything to reject. Identical
# counts are exactly what a working de-bounce produces here.
#
# What would discriminate: a period approaching 10 ms, i.e. a few hundred Hz.
# The counters are rated to 1 kHz max ("Max Frequency 1KHz" in the spec
# table), so the usable window is roughly 100-500 Hz. Above the rating the
# count under-reports SILENTLY and the driver cannot detect the overrun --
# which is why this was not pushed toward the limit unattended.
